name: Vikas
tagline: India's licensed Viking — three decades powering PSLV and GSLV
description: The Vikas traces directly to the French Viking engine: ISRO licensed the design in the 1970s and indigenised it at the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, adapting it for Indian manufacturing and progressively increasing performance through successive marks. Running a gas-generator cycle on nitrogen tetroxide and UDMH, Vikas first flew in September 1993 on PSLV and has since become the core liquid stage for PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3. It is the engine that powered Chandrayaan-1 to lunar orbit, Mangalyaan to Mars, and the Chandrayaan-3 mission that put Vikram on the Moon's south polar region.
best_known_for: India's workhorse — powers PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 to this day
